verses.text: Paul, Silvanus, and Timothy, to the church of the Thessalonians in God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ:
Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
Brothers and sisters, we should always thank God for you, as is right, because your faith is growing greatly and the love each of you has for one another keeps increasing.
That's why we proudly talk about you in God's churches: you stay strong and keep believing through all the persecution and hardships you're enduring.
All this shows that God's judgment is right, and that you will be counted worthy of God's Kingdom, for which you are suffering.
God is just: he will repay with trouble those who trouble you,
and give relief to you who are troubled, and to us too. This will happen when the Lord Jesus is revealed from heaven with his mighty angels
in blazing fire. He will punish those who don't know God and those who don't obey the Good News of our Lord Jesus.
They will suffer the punishment of eternal destruction, shut out from the Lord's presence and from his glorious power,
when he comes on that day to be glorified among his holy people and admired by all who believe. You believed our testimony to you.
With this in mind, we always pray for you, asking our God to make you worthy of his calling and to fulfill every good purpose and every work of faith through his power.
Then the name of our Lord Jesus will be honored in you, and you in him, through the grace of our God and the Lord Jesus Christ.
Brothers and sisters, about the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ and our gathering together to him, we ask you
not to become unsettled or alarmed by a spirit, a message, or a letter supposedly from us claiming that the day of the Lord has already arrived.
Don't let anyone deceive you in any way. That day won't come until the rebellion happens and the lawless one—the one headed for destruction—is revealed.
He will oppose and exalt himself over everything called a god or worshiped, even setting himself up in God's temple and claiming to be God.
Don't you remember I told you this when I was with you?
You know what is holding him back for now, so he can be revealed at the right time.
The hidden power of lawlessness is already at work. The one holding it back will keep doing so until he is taken out of the way.
Then the lawless one will be revealed. The Lord Jesus will kill him with the breath of his mouth and destroy him by the splendor of his coming.
The lawless one's coming will follow Satan's activity, with all kinds of power, signs, and lying wonders,
and every kind of evil deception for those who are perishing. They perish because they refused to love the truth and be saved.
For this reason, God lets a powerful delusion come over them, so they'll believe the lie
and be condemned—all those who refused to believe the truth and instead delighted in wrongdoing.

But we should always thank God for you, brothers and sisters loved by the Lord. God chose you from the beginning to be saved through the Spirit's work of making you holy and through your belief in the truth.
He called you to this through our Good News, so you could share in the glory of our Lord Jesus Christ.
So then, brothers and sisters, stand firm and hold on to the teachings we passed on to you, whether in person or by letter.
May our Lord Jesus Christ himself and God our Father, who loved us and gave us lasting comfort and a good hope through grace,
encourage your hearts and strengthen you in every good word and work.
Finally, brothers and sisters, pray for us, that the Lord's message will spread quickly and be honored, just as it was among you.
Pray that we will be rescued from unreasonable and evil people, because not everyone has faith.
But the Lord is faithful. He will strengthen you and protect you from the evil one.
We trust in the Lord that you're doing, and will keep doing, what we instructed.
May the Lord guide your hearts into God's love and Christ's endurance.
Brothers and sisters, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, we instruct you to stay away from any believer who lives idly and doesn't follow the teaching you received from us.
You know how you should imitate us. We didn't live idle lives among you.
We didn't accept anyone's food without paying. We worked hard night and day so we wouldn't burden any of you.
We did this not because we lacked the right to support, but to give you an example to follow.
Even when we were with you, we gave you this rule: ‘Anyone unwilling to work shouldn't eat.’
We hear that some among you are living idly. They're not working; they're just interfering in other people's business.
We instruct and urge such people in the Lord Jesus Christ to settle down, work, and earn their own food.
But you, brothers and sisters, don't get tired of doing what is right.
If anyone doesn't obey what we say in this letter, take note of them and don't associate with them, so they may feel ashamed.
Still, don't treat them as an enemy. Warn them as a brother or sister.
May the Lord of peace himself give you peace at all times and in every way. The Lord be with you all.
I, Paul, write this greeting in my own hand. This is how I mark every letter; this is my handwriting.
May the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen.
